newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index volume light, volatility up.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index volume light, volatility up.

text.p: Trading in major U.S. stock index options was on the light side despite a solid market rally, and traders said Tuesday volatility climbed higher after sliding last Friday ahead of a three-day weekend.
"Volatility went down to the lower end of its range but it's popped back up here," said Jack Callahan, an independent market maker in S&P 100 index options.
"It's come back even on an upward move here," he added. "Twenty volatility was too low to support what's going on in the market."
The Chicago Board Options Exchange's volatility index was up 1.38 points, or 6.75 percent, at 21.82, in afternoon activity.
Last Friday, the VIX reached its lowest level since early May. It is priced off certain OEX options.
The spot OEX was up 2.87 at 834.82 Tuesday afternoon after hitting a record 837.62 intraday.
Among broader indices, the S&P 500 index was ahead 1.78 at 848.81. It reached a record 851.53 intraday.
June S&P 500 futures rose 3.15 to 850.90.
Traders said the market was being supported mainly by strength in the technology sector, which helped propel the Nasdaq composite index .IXIC 16.02 points, or 1.15 percent, higher, to 1,405.74.
The Nasdaq composite reached an intraday high of 1,409, a record high.
The market's strength, in the face of a weak bond market and light activity, had some traders skeptical.

"I don't think anyone who is here believes this market is going anywhere because bonds are down and we're up only because we're following the techs," one S&P 500 futures options trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange said.
He said futures options trading was thin also and that volatilities there were up from Friday.
"Friday volatility was relatively crushed by the end of the day," he said. "But now we're coming back to the point where things are firming up."
A downside hedge by way of a June 675/725 put spread was one of the day's highlights, the trader said.
But he added that many of the large houses were mainly on the sidelines.
"Activity is kind of light," Callahan at the Chicago Board Options Exchange added. "There's a lot of wait-and-seeing, but the market's moving along anyhow."
In the OEX, the heaviest volume was in the June 840 calls, which traded 6,890 contracts. The June 790 and 830 puts also were active, with volume of about 4,690 contracts each.
